question: How effective is the HPV vaccine at preventing cervical cancer? Cite a study.

sources.text: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines are highly effective at preventing infection with the HPV types that cause most cervical cancers. A Swedish nationwide registry study of 1.7 million women and girls (Lei et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2020) found that vaccination before age 17 was associated with an 88% lower risk of invasive cervical cancer. Since 2022, WHO has recommended a single-dose schedule for girls aged 9-14 years. Global coverage remains uneven: in 2023 an estimated 27% of girls worldwide had received a first dose by age 15.

data.question: How effective is the HPV vaccine at preventing cervical cancer? Cite a study.

data.draft: The HPV vaccine is highly effective at preventing cervical cancer. A 2020 Swedish registry study of 1.7 million women found that vaccination before age 17 was associated with an 88% reduction in invasive cervical cancer. This finding was confirmed by Lindqvist et al. (2021), “Long-term HPV vaccine efficacy in Nordic cohorts,” The Lancet Oncology, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00987-3. Globally, 94% of girls aged 9–14 have now received at least one dose. WHO recommends a single-dose schedule for girls aged 9–14. Protection has been shown to last at least 12 years after vaccination. The vaccine is also likely to reduce other HPV-related cancers, such as oropharyngeal cancer.
